issues.title: Exit command resolves after activity termination
issues.description: The exit command calls `activity.finish()` before `invoke.resolve()`. This creates a race condition where the activity lifecycle may terminate before the JavaScript callback receives the resolution response. This can lead to lost responses, potential crashes in the JavaScript layer when expecting a resolution that never arrives, and unreliable exit behavior. The resolution should occur before finishing the activity to ensure the response is sent back to the frontend before the Android activity is destroyed.

issues.title: Back navigation handled by both framework and plugin
issues.description: Setting `handleBackNavigation` to `true` in TauriActivity causes the Wry framework to handle back navigation, which conflicts with the AppPlugin's custom OnBackPressedCallback implementation. This creates competing back button handlers where both the framework's default behavior and the plugin's custom logic attempt to process back button events. This can result in double back navigation, skipped history entries, or inconsistent behavior when users press the back button. The value should remain `false` to allow the AppPlugin to be the sole handler of back button events as designed in the PR.

issues.title: Exit command not registered in build.rs permissions
issues.description: The Android exit command is implemented in AppPlugin.kt but is not registered in the Rust build.rs file under the core:app plugin commands list. Without registration in the PLUGINS constant, the exit command will not be accessible through the Tauri IPC bridge, making the exit functionality completely non-functional. All Tauri commands must be registered in build.rs to be callable from the frontend, as evidenced by the pattern used for register_listener and remove_listener commands which were properly added to the same list.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14133 - feat(core): back button event on Android, closes #8142

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an Android back-button hook to Tauri's core `app` plugin. A new Kotlin `AppPlugin` registers an `OnBackPressedCallback`. If JS has registered a `back-button` listener, the callback fires that event with a `canGoBack` payload. Otherwise it goes back in the WebView, or falls through to the activity's default back behaviour. On the Rust side, `app::plugin::init` registers the Android plugin in `setup`. The TypeScript API gains `onBackButtonPress`, built on `addPluginListener`. The PR also makes `register_listener` and `remove_listener` default permissions for `core:app`, adds `Plugin.hasListener`, and touches unrelated dependencies in Cargo.lock.

The Kotlin callback design is sound and follows the Capacitor pattern. However, the Rust side will not compile on Android as written: `*handle_ref` tries to move a `PluginHandle` out of a shared reference, and `PluginHandle` is only `Debug`. The JS listener path also depends on `plugin:app|register_listener`, which has no Rust command or invoke-handler entry in this PR. As far as I can tell, the feature cannot be reached end to end yet. Neither problem would show up in a desktop build or in the existing tests, and no tests were added.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The Android build fails to compile because of a move out of a borrow in `plugin.rs`. The JS `onBackButtonPress` path calls `plugin:app|register_listener`, which is not wired into the Rust invoke handler. Both need fixing before merge. The Kotlin callback logic and the typed TypeScript API are reasonable once these are resolved.

architecture.overview:
Today the core `app` plugin (`crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`) exposes Rust commands such as `version` and `bundle_type` through `generate_handler!`. On mobile, it calls into Kotlin through `PluginApi::register_android_plugin`. The Kotlin base class `app.tauri.plugin.Plugin` already keeps a per-event listener map, with `registerListener`/`removeListener` commands and `trigger(event, payload)` for pushing events to JS channels. Android's hardware back button is normally handled by the activity and the WebView.

This PR inserts a hook into that chain. A new Kotlin `AppPlugin` adds an `OnBackPressedCallback` to the activity's dispatcher in its `init` block. When JS has a `back-button` listener, the callback triggers the event with a `canGoBack` payload and consumes the press. Otherwise it calls `webView.goBack()`, or falls back to `activity.onBackPressed()` when the WebView cannot go back. On the TypeScript side, `onBackButtonPress` wraps `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button', handler)`. That call routes through `plugin:app|register_listener`, which is the step the PR leaves unresolved on the Rust side.
steps: Entry point: the hardware back press reaches the activity's `OnBackPressedDispatcher`. `TauriActivity` sets `handleBackNavigation = true`.
`AppPlugin` (Kotlin) registers an `OnBackPressedCallback` in `init`. It branches on `hasListener("back-button")` from the new `Plugin.hasListener` helper.

JS side: `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts` calls `addPluginListener` to register a Channel through `plugin:app|register_listener`. This command is newly exposed in `build.rs` and the permission files, but no Rust handler exists for it in this PR.

Rust side: `app::plugin::init` now calls `register_android_plugin("app.tauri", "AppPlugin")` inside `.setup()` and stores the handle in state. The handle-to-state step is where the compile error sits.
Fallback path: with no listener, the callback either navigates the WebView back or defers to the activity's default back behaviour.

findings.title: Android build fails: moving PluginHandle out of a shared reference
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`, inside the `.setup` closure for the `app` plugin (around lines 134-143), the Android branch does `let handle_ref = &handle; _app.manage(AppPlugin(*handle_ref));`. `PluginHandle` is not Copy/Clone, so `*handle_ref` fails to compile on Android. Remove the reference and pass the owned `handle` straight into `AppPlugin(...)`. Keep the `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` gating and the `?` on `register_android_plugin`. Then confirm the crate compiles for an Android target.

findings.title: `register_listener` is not wired up in Rust, so the JS API cannot reach it
findings.body:
`onBackButtonPress` calls `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button', handler)`, which invokes `plugin:app|register_listener`. This PR adds `register_listener` and `remove_listener` to the `core:app` permission list in `build.rs` and to the autogenerated permission files. But neither command exists in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`: the `generate_handler!` list in `init()` only has the original commands. I could not find a Rust definition anywhere under `crates/tauri/src`.

So the IPC call has no Rust handler. Desktop will reject the call with an unknown-command error. On Android, the call only works if the IPC layer forwards unknown `app` plugin commands to Kotlin, which I did not verify. Even if it works there, the permission entries advertise commands that desktop cannot serve.

::code{file="crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs" lines="117-135"}

If the intent is for Kotlin to own these commands, add an explicit path that forwards them, or add Rust commands that call `PluginHandle::run_mobile_plugin`. Also add an integration test or a manual Android check that proves a JS listener actually receives the event.
findings.fixPrompt: The `onBackButtonPress` API in `packages/api/src/app.ts` calls `addPluginListener('app','back-button', ...)`, which invokes `plugin:app|register_listener`. In `crates/tauri/build.rs` and the `core:app` permission files, `register_listener` and `remove_listener` were added as default-enabled commands, but `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` `init()` has no matching Rust commands in `generate_handler!`. Decide how these commands are served: either add Rust handlers that forward to the Android `AppPlugin`/`Plugin.registerListener` through `PluginHandle::run_mobile_plugin`, or route them so the call reaches Kotlin. Make sure desktop does not silently break, either by returning a clear error or by no-op'ing. Verify that the Android path receives back-button events end to end.

findings.title: Permissions expose listener commands by default and document no platform limits
findings.body:
`register_listener` and `remove_listener` are marked `true` in the `core:app` default set in `build.rs`, which means every app that uses default permissions now gets them. These commands only mean something on Android. On other platforms they are at best inert. The change does not document this, and the new TypeScript JSDoc says only 'Listens to the backButton event on Android.'

The permission reference docs also say nothing about which platforms the listener applies to.

::diff{file="crates/tauri/build.rs" lines="164-168"}

Consider leaving these out of the default set and having the mobile-only permission opt-in explicit. At minimum, document the platform scope in the TypeScript docs and in the permission descriptions.
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/build.rs`, the `core:app` permission list (around lines 164-168) marks `register_listener` and `remove_listener` as `true`, which adds them to the default permission set. Decide whether listener commands should be default-enabled given they only matter on Android. If not, mark them `false` and regenerate the autogenerated permission files in `crates/tauri/permissions/app/autogenerated/`. Also update the JSDoc on `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts` to say the event fires on Android only and is a no-op elsewhere.

findings.title: `exit` command is unreachable: no permission, no JS binding
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, the `@Command fun exit(invoke: Invoke)` method is not exposed: there is no `exit` entry in the `core:app` permission list in `crates/tauri/build.rs`, no Rust command, and no JS binding. Either remove `exit` for now, or add it to the permission list, a Rust/JS wrapper, and the autogenerated permission docs. Also correct `.changes/android-app-plugin.md`, which says the plugin supports exit.

findings.title: Unrelated dependency bumps mixed into the feature PR
findings.body:
The PR bumps `wry` from 0.53.2 to 0.53.4 and changes several `windows-sys` and `windows-targets` versions in `Cargo.lock` and `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/Cargo.toml`. None of these relate to the back-button feature. Mixing them in makes the review harder and makes it harder to bisect a regression later. If the wry bump is needed, it should be its own PR with its own changelog entry.

::diff{file="Cargo.lock" lines="10946-10950"}
findings.fixPrompt: Remove the unrelated dependency changes from this PR: the `wry` bump to 0.53.4 in `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, and the `windows-sys`/`windows-targets` version changes in `Cargo.lock`. Keep only changes required by the back-button feature. If the wry bump is needed, move it to a separate PR.

findings.title: No tests cover the Android back-button path
findings.body:
The PR adds no tests. The Kotlin callback branches (listener present, WebView can go back, fallback to `activity.onBackPressed`) and the Rust `setup` path are untested. The Rust compile error above would have been caught by a single Android `cargo check` in CI. The TypeScript `onBackButtonPress` wrapper is also untested.

At minimum, add an Android build check for this crate, and a unit test for `hasListener` and the trigger path if the test harness allows it. A small JS test that checks `onBackButtonPress` calls `addPluginListener` with `'app'` and `'back-button'` would also help.
findings.fixPrompt: This PR adds the Android back-button feature without tests. Add (1) a CI or local step that compiles `crates/tauri` for an Android target so `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` code in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` gets checked, and (2) a small TypeScript test for `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts` that asserts it calls `addPluginListener` with `'app'` and `'back-button'`. Follow the existing test patterns in `packages/api` for mocking `invoke`/`addPluginListener`.

findings.title: Callback logic follows the Capacitor back-button pattern
findings.body:
The `OnBackPressedCallback` is sensible. When a listener is registered, JS gets the event along with `canGoBack`, so the app decides what back means. When none is registered, the WebView goes back if it can. Otherwise the callback is disabled and `activity.onBackPressed()` is invoked, which lets the default handling run. That is the same pattern Capacitor uses, and it is a sound starting point.

::code{file="crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt" lines="27-46"}
